(Golf Course Road only) gets "Yes" and a card.

findings.title: 'Is that a bestseller?' about a marked dish starts with 'No' and gives a made-up reason
findings.scenario: context.recommended=["menu:old-delhi-butter-chicken"], which is marked. Guest: "Is that a bestseller?" (EVIDENCE matches, so kind "evidence"). Reply: "No, we don't keep sales or popularity figures, ratings or reviews. I suggested the Old Delhi Butter Chicken because its menu description matched your request, and the restaurant marks it as a bestseller." (verified). The "No" contradicts the dish's own mark. When the dish came from a bestseller listing, "its menu description matched your request" is false.

findings.title: Bestsellers filtered out by stored price, avoid or exclude prefs produce 'None of the dishes ... is a dish.'
findings.scenario: Stored prefs {maxPrice:300} (or avoid nuts) and only dishes above ₹300 are marked. Guest: "what's your bestseller?" Reply: "None of the dishes the restaurant marks as bestsellers is a dish. I can suggest a dish that suits you instead." (verified). what(p) uses only the diet and the course, so the price or allergen that excluded the marked dishes is never mentioned and the sentence makes no sense.

findings.title: Bare 'popular' in SALES sends questions about busy times and branches to the dish bestseller answer
findings.scenario: "is it popular to book?", "Is Friday night popular? should I book ahead?" and "What's your most popular branch?" all return "sales". With dishes marked, the guest gets "The restaurant marks the Keema Pav Sliders and the Old Delhi Butter Chicken as bestsellers." plus dish cards. With none marked, they get "We don't keep sales or popularity figures, so I can't say which dish sells best." A grounded FAQ answer (walk-ins, booking window) is dropped unless the model happened to cite a faq: fact. REVIEWS has the same problem: "what's your hygiene rating?" and "Where can I leave a good review?" get "I can't say which dish is rated best".

verdicts.title: Popularity answers skip all allergy handling: unlisted allergens are not referred to staff and the allergy note is never shown
verdicts.evidence: Ran runTurn end to end in a scratch script: in-memory DB from evals/fixtures/base.json, sequenceModel, Kerala Prawn Curry and Yellow Dal Tadka marked. Input "I'm allergic to shellfish, what's your best seller?" (intent recommend or menu) gave prefs {allergy:true, unlisted:["shellfish"]} and the reply "The restaurant marks the Yellow Dal Tadka and the Kerala Prawn Curry as bestsellers." Blocks were [recommendation: Yellow Dal Tadka|Kerala Prawn Curry] with no notice. With Old Delhi Butter Chicken and Dal Ember marked, "What's your bestseller? I have a severe nut allergy" gave a Dal Ember card and no ALLERGY_NOTE. "I'm allergic to nuts, is the Old Delhi Butter Chicken popular?" gave "Yes: the restaurant marks the Old Delhi Butter Chicken as a bestseller." with a card for this nut-containing dish, again with no note. This held whether the model said recommend or faq. Causes: unmet() never looks at `unlisted`, evidenceStep never calls unlistedReferral, the named-dish branch never calls unmet, and routeTurn's recommend case adds no allergy block. recommendTurn (recommend.ts:630/635) and menuStep both do the referral and add the note.
verdicts.fix: In evidenceStep, return unlistedReferral(p) first when p.unlisted.length, check the named dish against unmet(p) before answering "Yes", and add the ALLERGY_NOTE notice when needsAllergyNote(p).

verdicts.title: EVIDENCE/REVIEWS regex captures safety, hours and policy questions and replaces the grounded answer with a canned 'No, we don't keep sales figures'
verdicts.evidence: evidenceQuestion() returns "evidence" for all six of the reviewer's inputs and for "Is there any evidence of a dress code?". End to end, a model faq answer citing hours:hauz-khas:sun for "You open at 12 on Sunday, is that right?" was replaced by "No, we don't keep sales or popularity figures, ratings or reviews. My suggestions come from the menu and what you tell me." (outcome recommend). A faq answer citing menu:paneer-lababdar for "How do you know the Paneer Lababdar is nut-free?" (context recommended=[yellow-dal-tadka], avoid nuts) became "No, ... I suggested the Yellow Dal Tadka because it fits what you asked for (dishes, without nuts)." with blocks [], so the guest is never told the dish contains nuts and no allergy note appears. "Do I need any proof of ID?" and "Do you keep any data about me?" with answerable=false got the same "No, we don't keep sales..." reply instead of the phone fallback. The turn.ts:486 bypass only applies to answerable faq answers that cite faq: or doc:.
verdicts.fix: Make EVIDENCE require a popularity or sales subject (or prior recommendation context with no safety or hours words), and let any answerable FAQ that passes grounding (hours:, menu:, branch:) through the bypass.

verdicts.title: HYPE_NEGATED treats 'which', 'if', 'any', 'whether', 'no', "can't" as negation, so hype claims about unmarked dishes pass (regression from the old HYPE_RE.exec check)
verdicts.evidence: Scratch run with only Old Delhi Butter Chicken marked: hypeClaims() returned [] for "Try the Dal Ember, which is a guest favourite, slow-cooked black lentils.", "You can't go wrong with the Dal Ember, our most popular dish of slow-cooked black lentils.", "No visit is complete without our famous Kulfi.", "Whether you want rich or light, the Kulfi is a must-try." and "The Dal Makhani, if you ask me, is our signature dish." As a control, "Try the Dal Ember, our most popular dish." returned ['most popular']. validateChoice(pick dal-ember) returned reasons [] for the first two replies but rejected the control. Before this commit, e065050 recommend.ts:333/377 used HYPE_RE.exec(reply), which matches 'favou?rites?' and 'most popular' and would have rejected both. The same filter feeds claimProblems (recommend.ts:331) and plan.ts safeNote (line 140).
verdicts.fix: Limit HYPE_NEGATED to real negators that govern the claim (e.g. "don't track|can't say|no (?:sales|data)"), and drop which/if/any/whether and the bare 'no'/'can't go wrong'.

verdicts.title: A bestseller claim is accepted if any shown or cited dish is marked, not the dish the claim is about
verdicts.evidence: Scratch run with only Old Delhi Butter Chicken marked: validateChoice({pick:'menu:dal-ember', alternatives:['menu:old-delhi-butter-chicken'], reply:'The Dal Ember is our bestseller, slow-cooked black lentils; the Old Delhi Butter Chicken is richer.'}) returned []. Without the alternative, the same claim is rejected. claimProblems('The Dal Ember is our bestseller. The Old Delhi Butter Chicken is in a tomato, butter and cashew gravy.', cited [dal-ember, butter-chicken]) returned [], because citedText holds the butter chicken's 'Marked as a bestseller by the restaurant.' Line 462 uses shown.some(d => d.bestseller), and line 331 tests the regex against all cited text.
verdicts.fix: Find the claim's dish with subjectAt(match index) and require that dish's bestseller flag (in claimProblems, the mark in that dish's own fact).

verdicts.title: A review or rating question about a named marked dish is answered 'Yes', which invents reviews
verdicts.evidence: Scratch runTurn with Old Delhi Butter Chicken marked: "Does the Old Delhi Butter Chicken have good reviews?" and "Is the Old Delhi Butter Chicken well rated?" both have kind 'reviews'. Both returned "Yes: the restaurant marks the Old Delhi Butter Chicken as a bestseller." with a recommendation card. The named-dish branch (line 58-60) runs for any kind except 'evidence', so it is reached before the reviews branch's "We don't collect reviews or ratings".
verdicts.fix: In the named-dish branch, when kind === 'reviews', start with "We don't collect reviews or ratings" and then mention the mark, never "Yes".

verdicts.title: Named-dish popularity answer ignores availability and branch, so an unavailable or other-branch dish is recommended
verdicts.evidence: Scratch runTurn with tandoori-pomfret (isAvailable:false) and keema-pav-sliders (branches:[gurugram]) marked. "Is the Tandoori Pomfret popular?" returned "Yes: the restaurant marks the Tandoori Pomfret as a bestseller." with a card, and context.recommended=['menu:tandoori-pomfret']. Nothing said it is unavailable. "Is the Keema Pav Sliders popular at Hauz Khas?" (branchNamed=hauz-khas) returned "Yes: ..." with a card for a dish served only at Golf Course Road. `named` is matched against all input.entries, while `marked` filters e.available && servedAt.
verdicts.fix: Before saying "Yes" for a named dish, check d.available and servedAt(d, branch); otherwise say it is currently unavailable or not served at that branch, and add no card or recommended id.

verdicts.title: 'Is that a bestseller?' about a marked dish starts with 'No' and gives a made-up reason
verdicts.evidence: Scratch runTurn with butter chicken marked and context.recommended=['menu:old-delhi-butter-chicken']. "Is that a bestseller?" and "Is that really popular?" (kind 'evidence') both returned "No, we don't keep sales or popularity figures, ratings or reviews. I suggested the Old Delhi Butter Chicken because its menu description matched your request, and the restaurant marks it as a bestseller." The leading "No" contradicts the mark stated at the end. The "menu description matched" reason is hard-coded whenever prefs are empty, including when the dish came from a bestseller listing.
verdicts.fix: When `last` is marked, answer "Yes, the restaurant marks the X as a bestseller" (then say there are no sales figures), and only give the description reason when it is true.

verdicts.title: Bestsellers filtered out by stored price, avoid or exclude prefs produce 'None of the dishes ... is a dish.'
verdicts.evidence: Scratch runTurn with butter chicken (₹645) and Dal Ember (₹445, contains dairy) marked. With context prefs {maxPrice:300}, "what's your bestseller?" returned "None of the dishes the restaurant marks as bestsellers is a dish. I can suggest a dish that suits you instead." With {avoid:['dairy']}, the reply was the same sentence. what(p) uses only diet and course, so the price or allergen that ruled the dishes out is never mentioned.
verdicts.fix: Build the none-fit sentence from describePrefs(p), e.g. "None of the dishes the restaurant marks as bestsellers is <describePrefs(p)>", or name the constraint that excluded them.

verdicts.title: Bare 'popular' in SALES sends questions about busy times and branches to the dish bestseller answer
verdicts.evidence: evidenceQuestion returned 'sales' for "is it popular to book?", "Is Friday night popular? should I book ahead?" and "What's your most popular branch?". It returned 'reviews' for "what's your hygiene rating?" and "Where can I leave a good review?". With two dishes marked and the model returning answerable=false, "Is Friday night popular? should I book ahead?" and "What's your most popular branch?" both got "The restaurant marks the Old Delhi Butter Chicken and the Dal Ember as bestsellers." plus dish cards. "what's your hygiene rating?" got "We don't collect reviews or ratings, so I can't say which dish is rated best. ..." with cards. With nothing marked, "is it popular to book?" got "We don't keep sales or popularity figures, so I can't say which dish sells best...". An answerable faq citing faq: does go to the FAQ path. Answers citing hours: or nothing, and answerable=false, are replaced.
verdicts.fix: Remove bare `popular(?:ity)?` from SALES (or require a dish, food or course noun nearby), and make REVIEWS require a dish or food context word.

findings.title: An allergy stated in a meal-plan message is ignored: dishes are not filtered, no allergy note is shown, and the allergy is never saved
findings.scenario: New conversation, guest types "Can 2 of us eat here under ₹1,500? We eat everything, but I am allergic to nuts." explicitPrefs reads {allergy:true, avoid:[nuts]}, but step 3b calls planTurn with prefs = prefsOut, which is still the stored context prefs (empty here). readPlanRequest only uses maxPrice. So planDishes does not remove nut dishes, and validatePlan never checks allergens. I ran this through planTurn in a scratch script: a planner reply of Paneer Lababdar + Old Delhi Butter Chicken was accepted, with the reply "Here's a meal for two people that comes to ₹1,170, within your ₹1,500." Both dishes contain dairy and nuts. The blocks were [meal_plan, quick_replies] with no ALLERGY_NOTE notice, and the router's recommend case adds none. prefsOut is never updated on this path, so the returned context has no allergy, and later recommendations and menus also forget it.

findings.title: Mixed veg/non-veg groups are read as diet "any", so no vegetarian main is required and no question is asked
findings.scenario: planDietIn checks for meat words before it looks for mixed groups described with numbers. Results from a scratch run: "Two of us are vegetarian and one eats chicken" gives any; "2 veg, 1 non-veg" gives any; "My wife is vegetarian, I eat meat" gives any; "Two vegetarians and one non-vegetarian" gives any. readPlanRequest("Can 3 of us eat here under ₹2,000? Two of us are vegetarian and one eats chicken.") returns diet "any". Because the diet is not null, the diet question is skipped, and validatePlan only requires a vegetarian main when diet is "mixed". A plan of Malai Chicken Tikka + Chicken Chettinad + Lamb Seekh Kebab passes and is shown to a group where two people are vegetarian.

findings.title: The plan diet question is asked only once per conversation, but the answer is never saved, so later plans default to "any" and ignore a stored vegetarian preference
findings.scenario: Turn 1 "Can 2 of us eat under ₹1,000?" asks the diet question and adds asked:[plan_diet]. Turn 2 "All vegetarian" gives a vegetarian plan. The diet lives only in context.plan; prefsOut is not updated. Turn 3 is the menu chip, which drops context.plan. Turn 4 "Can 3 of us eat here under ₹2,000?" has focus.diet null and input.asked true, so the question is skipped and diet becomes "any". planDishes (line 90) also ignores prefs.diet. I verified this with planTurn(asked:true, prefs.diet:["vegetarian"]): a plan of Malai Chicken Tikka + Chicken Chettinad + Dal Ember was accepted and shown to a guest who had said they were vegetarian.

findings.title: The branch chips for a weekday hours question drop the weekday, which hides that day's closures and special hours
findings.scenario: Fixture data, now = 2026-10-21. A guest asks "What are your hours on Tuesdays?" readHoursQuestion returns weekday:2. Golf Course Road's section has a note for the Tue 27 Oct all-day closure, so the cards don't merge and the reply is "Which branch? Hauz Khas and Golf Course Road keep different hours." That is untrue: their Tuesday hours are the same. The chips are {type:"hours",branch:"gurugram"}, and ActionSchema (types.ts:57) has no weekday or meal field. Tapping Golf Course Road gives "Here are the regular opening hours at Golf Course Road." with a full-week card that shows lunch and dinner as open and never mentions "Closed all day for kitchen maintenance" on Tue 27 Oct. Typing "hours at Golf Course Road on Tuesdays" does show that note. HoursFocus has no weekday either, so typing the branch name as the answer loses it too. The same happens for Saturdays: the 31 Oct extended dinner hours are lost.

findings.title: A per-person budget times the party can go past the ContextSchema budget limit of 200,000, and the next request then fails with a 400 every time
findings.scenario: "Can 10 of us eat here for ₹25k per person?" makes readPlanRequest (plan.ts:82) return budget 250000, basis per_person. "Can 12 of us eat for ₹20,000 each?" gives 240000, and "under ₹60,000 per person" for 4 gives 240000. planTurn asks the diet question and returns that focus. runTurn copies it into context.plan with no output check, the client saves it, and every later message sends it back. ChatBodySchema then fails with 400 VALIDATION ("plan.budget: Too big"). The client shows "Try again", which resends the same context, so the chat keeps failing until Start over or New conversation. I confirmed with ContextSchema.safeParse that it returns success:false.

findings.title: The meal plan card leaves out a dish's branch-only note, so a plan can include a dish the guest's branch doesn't serve
findings.scenario: No branch chosen yet (draft.branch null). planDishes calls eligible with branch null, so Keema Pav Sliders (Golf Course Road only) is allowed. In a scratch run, planTurn accepted keema-pav-sliders + dal-ember + chicken-chettinad (₹1,595), and the item's scope was "Golf Course Road only". DishRow and DishCard show item.scope, but MealPlan shows only courseLabel, labels and contains. A guest planning a Hauz Khas visit sees a ₹1,595 plan that they can't order there.

findings.title: Right after a plan, a question about a dish or a request to come in is read as a change to the plan, and the meal is planned again
findings.scenario: context.plan = {party 2, budget 1500, diet any}. "Is the chana pindi vegan?" gives diet vegan, changed, and a whole new vegan meal plan instead of an answer. "Is the dal vegetarian?" does the same with a vegetarian plan. "Great, we'd like to come tonight for 4" reads party 4 and plans again for four. BOOKING_WORDS (line 47) lacks come/visit, which guards' BOOKING_CUE_RE includes, so the guest gets a meal plan instead of the booking flow. All three verified with readPlanRequest.

findings.title: "One of us has ..." is read as a party of 1, so a follow-up plans a meal for one person

verdicts.title: An allergy stated in a meal-plan message is ignored: dishes are not filtered, no allergy note is shown, and the allergy is never saved
verdicts.evidence: I ran it end to end with runTurn (in-memory DB, base.json, scripted model). Guest message: "Can 2 of us eat here under ₹1,500? We eat everything, but I am allergic to nuts." The reply was "Here's a meal for two people that comes to ₹1,170, within your ₹1,500." The meal_plan held menu:paneer-lababdar and menu:old-delhi-butter-chicken, both contains [dairy, nuts]. Blocks were [meal_plan, quick_replies] with no ALLERGY_NOTE notice. The returned context had prefs:null, no allergyNoted, and plan.diet "any". The planner prompt had no "Avoid:" line. Cause: turn.ts:319 passes prefs: prefsOut ?? noPrefs(), which is only the stored prefs. explicitPrefs(latest) returns {allergy:true, avoid:["nuts"]} but readPlanRequest only uses its maxPrice. The router's recommend case adds no allergy note. When I fed those prefs into planDishes, it did drop paneer-lababdar, so the filter works once it gets the allergy.
verdicts.fix: In step 3b, merge explicitPrefs(latest) (avoid, allergy, unlisted, diet) into prefsOut before planTurn and send unlistedReferral when it applies. Pass the merged prefs to planTurn and add the ALLERGY_NOTE notice when needsAllergyNote is true and the note hasn't been shown yet.

verdicts.title: Mixed veg/non-veg groups are read as diet "any", so no vegetarian main is required and no question is asked
verdicts.evidence: In a scratch run, planDietIn gave: "Two of us are vegetarian and one eats chicken" -> any, "2 veg, 1 non-veg" -> any, "My wife is vegetarian, I eat meat" -> any, "Two vegetarians and one non-vegetarian" -> any. Only the literal "one of us is vegetarian and the other..." and "mix" gave mixed. The mixed regex at plan.ts:39 only covers one/some (of us) is/are veg. Then line 41 matches eats chicken, eat meat or non-veg and returns any. readPlanRequest("Can 3 of us eat here under ₹2,000? Two of us are vegetarian and one eats chicken.") returned diet "any". planTurn accepted Malai Chicken Tikka + Chicken Chettinad + Lamb Seekh Kebab (₹1,895) with no rejection reasons, because validatePlan only requires a veg main when diet is "mixed".
verdicts.fix: In planDietIn, return "mixed" when the text has both a veg word (veg, vegetarian, vegan) and a meat or non-veg word. Run that check before the "any" match.

verdicts.title: The plan diet question is asked only once per conversation, but the answer is never saved, so later plans default to "any" and ignore a stored vegetarian preference
verdicts.evidence: I ran the turns in order through runTurn. T1 "Can 2 of us eat under ₹1,000?" asked the diet question and set asked:[plan_diet]. T2 "All vegetarian" gave a vegetarian plan, but context.prefs stayed null. T3, the menu chip, returned a context without plan, because planOut is only set on the plan path. T4 "Can 3 of us eat here under ₹2,000?" asked no question and accepted Malai Chicken Tikka + Chicken Chettinad + Dal Ember with plan.diet "any". In a separate run with context.prefs.diet ["vegetarian"] and asked [plan_diet], the same non-veg plan was accepted. planDishes (plan.ts:91) builds diet only from focus.diet and ignores prefs.diet. planTurn line 184 sets the diet to "any" once asked is true.
verdicts.fix: When focus.diet is null, take it from prefs.diet (vegetarian or vegan) before using "any". Also save the plan diet answer into prefsOut.diet, or ask again whenever the diet is unknown, instead of falling back to "any".

verdicts.title: The branch chips for a weekday hours question drop the weekday, which hides that day's closures and special hours
verdicts.evidence: Fixture data, now 2026-10-21. readHoursQuestion("What are your hours on Tuesdays?") gave {branches:null, weekday:2}. hoursAnswer replied "Which branch? Hauz Khas and Golf Course Road keep different hours." with chips {type:"hours",branch:"hauz-khas"} and {type:"hours",branch:"gurugram"}, so no weekday is carried. Both branches' Tuesday rows are the same (12:00 PM – 3:30 PM and 7:00 PM – 11:00 PM). Only Golf Course Road's note "Special hours on Tue 27 Oct: closed all day." differs, so the question's claim is misleading. Tapping the Golf Course Road chip through runTurn (turn.ts:248 hard-codes weekday:null) gave "Here are the regular opening hours at Golf Course Road." with a full-week card and no 27 Oct note. Typing "hours at Golf Course Road on Tuesdays" does show the note. Same for Saturdays: the Hauz Khas chip gives an "Every day" card without "Special hours on Sat 31 Oct: dinner 7:00 PM – 11:30 PM (Extended dinner hours)". ActionSchema and HoursFocus have no weekday field.
verdicts.fix: Add an optional weekday (0-6) to the hours ActionSchema and to HoursFocus. Put it on the branch chips in hoursAnswer, and pass chip.weekday (or focus.weekday) into the question at turn.ts:248 and in readHoursQuestion.

verdicts.title: A per-person budget times the party can go past the ContextSchema budget limit of 200,000, and the next request then fails with a 400 every time
verdicts.evidence: readPlanRequest gave budget 250000 for "Can 10 of us eat here for ₹25k per person?", 240000 for "Can 12 of us eat for ₹20,000 each?" and 240000 for "Can 4 of us eat here under ₹60,000 per person?". Running the first through runTurn returned the diet question with context.plan.budget 250000. ContextSchema.safeParse on that context failed: plan.budget too_big, max 200000. ChatBodySchema.safeParse on the next message with that context also failed. ChatPanel saves r.context as is and resends it, and Try again resends the same context, so every message fails until Start over.
verdicts.fix: In readPlanRequest, cap the budget to the schema limit, or treat amount*party > 200000 as not a plan request. Or raise the ContextSchema limit to cover PARTY_MAX × the per-person cap.

verdicts.title: The meal plan card leaves out a dish's branch-only note, so a plan can include a dish the guest's branch doesn't serve
verdicts.evidence: With branch null, planTurn accepted keema-pav-sliders + dal-ember + chicken-chettinad (₹1,595). The block item had scope "Golf Course Road only". MealPlan in Blocks.tsx (the new component at lines ~343-390) renders courseLabel, Labels (dietary labels only) and contains, but not item.scope. DishCard (line 263) and DishRow (line 290) do render scope. The reply line doesn't name a branch either. With branch "hauz-khas" the dish is filtered out (servedAt), so this only happens when no branch is known.
verdicts.fix: In MealPlan, render item.scope next to the Contains line, as DishRow does.

verdicts.title: Right after a plan, a question about a dish or a request to come in is read as a change to the plan, and the meal is planned again
verdicts.evidence: With prev = {party 2, budget 1500, diet any}, readPlanRequest returned changed:true for "Is the chana pindi vegan?" (diet vegan), "Is the dal vegetarian?" (diet vegetarian) and "Great, we'd like to come tonight for 4" (party 4). runTurn step 3b runs before retrieval and the intent call, so each of these gets a new meal plan instead of an FAQ answer or the booking flow. BOOKING_WORDS (plan.ts:47) lacks the come, coming, visit and seat words that guards' BOOKING_CUE_RE has. A plain question like "what time do you open tomorrow?" is correctly left alone.
verdicts.fix: In follow-up mode, skip questions (a leading is, does or can, or a trailing ?) that name a dish, and messages with booking cues (use BOOKING_CUE_RE). Treat a diet word alone as a change only when the message isn't about a named dish.

verdicts.title: "One of us has ..." is read as a party of 1, so a follow-up plans a meal for one person
verdicts.evidence: readPlanRequest("We eat everything, but one of us has a nut allergy", prev{party 2, diet null}) returned focus {party:1, diet:any}. The strip regex at plan.ts:26 covers only is/are/eats/doesn't/don't/can't, so partyStated matches "one of us" and returns 1. With no prior plan, "There are 4 of us and one of us has a nut allergy. Can we eat here under ₹3,000?" and "Can 4 of us eat here under ₹3,000? One of us has a nut allergy." both returned null, because the last match (1) gives party < 2. The planning request is dropped.
verdicts.fix: In partyIn, remove every "(one|some|two|...) of us" phrase not preceded by "there are" or "we are", or ignore partyStated matches of 1 from "one of us"; and keep prev.party when the parsed party is 1 in a follow-up.

verdicts.title: The new hours date fields check only the YYYY-MM-DD pattern, not that the date is real, so an invalid date gets past validation and crashes the turn
verdicts.evidence: ActionSchema.safeParse({type:"hours",branch:"gurugram",date:"2026-02-30"}) and ContextSchema.safeParse({lastCitedIds:[],hours:{branches:["gurugram"],date:"2026-99-99"}}) both returned true. runTurn with that action threw RangeError "invalid local date: 2026-02-30" (and 2026-99-99). lib/api/chat.ts doesn't catch it, so the request ends in a 500 instead of a 400. Only a forged or corrupted request reaches this, since server-made chips carry valid dates. DraftSchema already uses refine(isLocalDate).
verdicts.fix: Use z.string().refine(isLocalDate) for ActionSchema hours.date (types.ts:57) and ContextSchema hours.date (types.ts:102).

verdicts.title: Likely at 360px: the "Special hours this day" badge is a plain inline span and can break across two lines
verdicts.evidence:
The wrap would happen. Container math at 360px: 328 after page px-4, minus the 32px avatar and 10px gap, minus the card's border and px-4, leaves about 252px. Avenir Next metrics (PIL): "Tomorrow, Thu 22 Oct" at 13px is 135px and the badge is 118+16 = 134px, so 135+8+134 = 277px > 252. The

wraps under the heading, and the inline badge then breaks after "this". "Today, Wed 21 Oct" (114px) gives 256px, which also just overflows. A plain "Thu 22 Oct" fits. But this is cosmetic only: no horizontal overflow (the e2e noOverflow check still holds), the text stays whole and readable, and nothing a guest relies on is wrong or hidden. It falls under the task's "no style nits" rule, not a real defect.
